newsitem.title: USA: Warm weather, sunshine help Iowa corn and soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Warm weather, sunshine help Iowa corn and soybeans.

text.p: Above normal temperatures and sunny skies aided Iowa corn and soybean crops and conditions for both improved slightly in the week ended Sunday, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said.
Corn was rated one percent very poor, four percent poor, 20 percent fair, 56 percent good and 19 percent excellent.
Soybeans were rated one percent very poor, five percent poor, 25 fair, 53 percent good and 16 percent excellent.
But progress still lagged average with 64 percent of the corn in the dough stage, compared with 72 percent on average and 78 percent last year.
Twenty percent of the crop had reached the dent stage, behind average of 44 and last year's pace of 47 percent.
There were reports of second-generation corn borers in the north-central district.
Leaves were turning color on four percent of the soybean acreage, compared with the average of 14 percent, while 96 percent had set pods, nearly in line with average of 97 percent.
White mold was reported in northwest, west central and central districts.
Soil moisture was rated three percent very short, 18 percent short, 76 percent adequate and three percent surplus.
Pasture was rated three percent very poor, 15 percent poor, 30 percent fair, 45 percent good and seven percent excellent.
